artifacts.summary: Draft specification shared in a shared doc

items.text:
## Summary

Internal draft of the Real‑time Inference API spec, detailing latency tiers, payload limits, hardware and model adjustments, and the confidential beta performance metrics that will inform the planned launch.

## 1. Overview & Launch Context

This document captures the current draft of the Real‑time Inference API specification for the feature launch scheduled on **day 35**. The API will expose a low‑latency endpoint at `https://api.internal/realtime` for internal consumption only. Julia Kim (Product Manager) and Karen Lee (Senior ML Engineer) prepared the draft; Keira Lindqvist (Head of Product) has reviewed it. No formal decision on the final release has been recorded yet.

## 2. API Contract – Request Format & Latency Targets

The API accepts a **JSON** payload with a single top‑level field named `"input"`. The payload size is limited to **2 KB**. Two service tiers are defined:

- **Standard tier** – 95th‑percentile latency ≤ **8 ms** at **10 k RPS**.
- **Premium tier** – 95th‑percentile latency ≤ **4 ms** at **10 k RPS**.

These targets match the latency table discussed on 2026‑02‑05. Karen Lee confirmed feasibility for the standard tier and highlighted the need for additional optimizations to meet the premium target.

## 3. Performance & Capacity Planning

To satisfy the premium tier latency goal, Karen Lee recommends two mitigations (recorded in the restricted draft folder):

1. **Add two A100‑GPU nodes**, providing roughly a **20 % capacity boost**. This will lower the projected GPU utilization from **~85 %** to under **80 %** when the premium workload runs at the target latency.
2. **Prune the model by ~10 %**. The reduction keeps GPU utilization under the 80 % threshold but will decrease the maximum RPS for the premium tier by about **15 %** if we remain on the existing hardware pool.

Beta testing reported a **median latency of 3.8 ms** and a **95th‑percentile latency of 4.6 ms**. These metrics are stored in the restricted draft folder and will be used to validate the hardware‑model trade‑off.

Julia Kim will incorporate these notes into the next spec iteration and will flag any further hardware or model‑size adjustments required to stay within the latency‑throughput envelope.

## 4. Confidential Artefacts & Review Process

All detailed latency trade‑off analyses, hardware sizing calculations, and beta metrics are saved in the **restricted draft folder** (keep within the team). Access is limited to Julia Kim, Karen Lee, and Keira Lindqvist. The next review cycle will be conducted by the same trio, after which the spec will be circulated to the broader product engineering group for a security and compliance sign‑off. No external distribution is permitted until a formal launch decision is recorded.

items.text:
## Description

### Objective
Create the production‑ready low‑latency inference endpoint described in the draft specification (see `/shared/real_time_inference/restricted_draft/Realtime_API_Spec_v1.md` – ****). The implementation must satisfy the two latency tiers:
- **Standard tier** – 95th‑percentile ≤ **8 ms** at **10 k RPS**
- **Premium tier** – 95th‑percentile ≤ **4 ms** at **10 k RPS**

### Required actions
1. **Hardware provisioning** – Karen Lee will provision **two additional A100‑GPU nodes** (≈ 20 % capacity boost) and update the cluster definition in `/infra/gpu_cluster/config.yaml` (**restricted draft folder**). Expected impact: GPU utilization drops from ~85 % to < 80 % for premium workloads.
2. **Model adjustment** – Karen Lee will prune the current model by **~10 %** (recorded in the same config file) and generate a new model artifact at `/models/realtime/v2/model_pruned.pt` (****). This step will reduce the premium tier max RPS by ~15 % on the existing pool.
3. **API contract implementation** – Julia Kim will coordinate the service code changes in `/srv/api/realtime/` to enforce the **2 KB JSON payload** limit (field `"input"`). Unit tests will verify payload size and JSON schema.
4. **Performance validation** – After hardware and model updates, Karen Lee will run a latency benchmark suite (`/tools/benchmark/realtime_latency_test.sh`) and store the results in `/shared/real_time_inference/restricted_draft/benchmark_results_20260211.json` (**keep within the team**). The suite must confirm median ≤ 3.8 ms and 95th‑percentile ≤ 4.6 ms for the premium tier before moving to production.
5. **Spec revision** – Julia Kim will incorporate the final hardware and model numbers into the specification document and move the updated spec to `/shared/real_time_inference/final/Realtime_API_Spec_Final.md` (**restricted draft folder**). Keira Lindqvist will review the revised spec for product alignment.
6. **Endpoint rollout** – Once validation passes, the endpoint will be exposed at `https://api.internal/realtime` (****) behind the internal load balancer. Configuration changes go in `/srv/api/realtime/nginx.conf` and will be deployed via the CI pipeline defined in `/ci/pipelines/realtime_api.yml`.

### Documentation & Artefacts
All latency trade‑off analyses, hardware sizing calculations, and beta metrics remain in the **restricted draft folder**. Access is limited to Julia Kim, Karen Lee, and Keira Lindqvist. No external distribution is permitted until a formal launch decision is recorded.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two A100‑GPU nodes are added and reflected in the cluster config file.
- Model is pruned by ~10 % and the new artifact is stored at the path specified.
- API rejects any request payload > 2 KB and returns a 400 error.
- Benchmark suite reports median latency ≤ 3.8 ms and 95th‑percentile ≤ 4.6 ms for premium tier workloads.
- Updated spec document passes Keira Lindqvist’s product review.
- CI pipeline successfully deploys the endpoint to `https://api.internal/realtime` without errors.
- All changes are committed to the restricted draft folder and no artefacts are leaked outside the authorised team.

items.text:
## Background

The Real‑time Inference API feature has progressed through a series of technical reviews and a formal sign‑off meeting. On 2026‑02‑05 Julia Kim circulated a latency target table that defines two service tiers: Standard tier ≤ 8 ms 95th‑percentile at 10 k RPS and Premium tier ≤ 4 ms at 10 k RPS, with a JSON payload limited to 2 KB. Karen Lee confirmed feasibility for the Standard tier and identified the need for tighter kernel‑level batching to meet the Premium target, noting that GPU utilization would rise above 80 % without mitigation.

Karen’s detailed hardware‑capacity analysis (uploaded to the restricted draft folder) proposes adding two A100‑GPU nodes – roughly a 20 % capacity boost – and pruning the model by ~10 % to keep GPU utilization under 80 % for Premium workloads. The trade‑off reduces the Premium tier’s maximum RPS by about 15 % on the existing pool.

Beta testing results stored in the same restricted draft folder show a median latency of 3.8 ms and a 95th‑percentile latency of 4.6 ms, confirming that the hardware‑model adjustments can satisfy the Premium target.

The draft specification ("Draft Real‑time Inference API Specification – Internal Review") was authored by Julia Kim (Product Manager) and Karen Lee (Senior ML Engineer) and reviewed by Keira Lindqvist (Head of Product). The spec lives at `/shared/real_time_inference/restricted_draft/Realtime_API_Spec_v1.md` and references the internal endpoint URL `https://api.internal/realtime`.

During the sign‑off meeting on 2026‑02‑16, Keira Lindqvist reviewed the latency and capacity plan, confirmed the spec alignment with beta metrics, and gave the final approval: **Approve real‑time inference API launch**. Action items were recorded with owners and due dates: Julia Kim will finalize the deployment pipeline by 2026‑02‑23, coordinate hardware provisioning and model pruning by 2026‑02‑28, and run the final benchmark suite by 2026‑02‑26; Keira Lindqvist will update public‑facing documentation by 2026‑02‑27. All artefacts remain in the restricted draft folder until release.

## Recommendation

Proceed with the launch as approved by Keira Lindqvist (Head of Product). The deployment pipeline should be completed by 2026‑02‑23, after which the endpoint will be rolled out on day 35. The two additional A100‑GPU nodes must be provisioned and the model pruned by ~10 % (as detailed in `/infra/gpu_cluster/config.yaml` and `/models/realtime/v2/model_pruned.pt`). Once hardware and model changes are in place, Julia Kim will enforce the 2 KB JSON payload limit in `/srv/api/realtime/` and verify that oversized requests return HTTP 400. The final benchmark suite (`/tools/benchmark/realtime_latency_test.sh`) must confirm median latency ≤ 3.8 ms and 95th‑percentile ≤ 4.6 ms for the Premium tier before the launch date. After these conditions are satisfied, the API can be made publicly available to internal consumers on the scheduled launch day.

## Conditions

- Two A100‑GPU nodes added and reflected in `/infra/gpu_cluster/config.yaml` by 2026‑02‑28.
- Model pruned by ~10 % and new artifact stored at `/models/realtime/v2/model_pruned.pt` by 2026‑02‑28.
- Deployment pipeline finalized and approved by Julia Kim by 2026‑02‑23.
- Final performance benchmark run by Julia Kim by 2026‑02‑26, with results meeting median ≤ 3.8 ms and 95th‑percentile ≤ 4.6 ms for Premium tier (results archived in the restricted draft folder).
- Public‑facing documentation updated to reflect latency targets, payload limit, and launch timing by Keira Lindqvist by 2026‑02‑27.
- All changes and artefacts remain in the restricted draft folder until the launch; no external distribution is permitted.

items.text:
## Summary

This release‑notes brief records the final approval and the concrete rollout plan for the Real‑time Inference API, including latency targets, hardware upgrades, and deployment responsibilities.

## Release Summary

The Real‑time Inference API launch has received the final decision **Approve real‑time inference API launch** from **Keira Lindqvist, Head of Product**. The feature will be made available to internal consumers on **day 35** via the endpoint `https://api.internal/realtime`. All public‑facing documentation will be updated to reflect the final latency targets and payload limits before the launch.

## Key Technical Specs

* **Latency tiers** – Standard tier 95th‑percentile ≤ 8 ms at 10 k RPS; Premium tier 95th‑percentile ≤ 4 ms at 10 k RPS. * **Payload limit** – JSON body with a single `"input"` field, maximum size **2 KB**. * **Hardware & model adjustments** – Two additional A100‑GPU nodes (≈ 20 % capacity boost) and a ~10 % model prune will keep premium‑tier GPU utilization below 80 %. * **Beta performance** – Median latency **3.8 ms**, 95th‑percentile **4.6 ms**. * **Endpoint** – Internal URL `https://api.internal/realtime` enforces the 2 KB limit and returns HTTP 400 for oversized requests.

## Deployment Timeline & Responsibilities

| Milestone | Owner | Due |
|— |— |— |
| Lock deployment pipeline for rollout gate | **Julia Kim** (Product Manager) | 2026-02-23 |
| Provision two A100‑GPU nodes & update `/infra/gpu_cluster/config.yaml` | **Karen Lee** (Senior ML Engineer) | 2026-02-28 |
| Prune model and store new artifact at `/models/realtime/v2/model_pruned.pt` | **Karen Lee** | 2026-02-28 |
| Run final benchmark suite (`/tools/benchmark/realtime_latency_test.sh`) and archive results | **Julia Kim** | 2026-02-26 |
| Update public‑facing documentation with final latency targets and payload limit | **Keira Lindqvist** (Head of Product) | 2026-02-27 |
All artifacts (hardware config, model file, benchmark results, release manifest) remain in the **restricted draft folder** (keep within the team) until the launch day.

## Confidentiality & Distribution

This document is a **draft review copy** intended solely for the product and engineering leads (Julia Kim, Karen Lee, Keira Lindqvist). It must not be forwarded outside this group or used in any customer‑facing material until the official public announcement is approved. All sensitive values—launch day, internal endpoint URL, and beta latency metrics—are marked **confidential** and stored in the restricted folder.
